events.title: Henry IV Claims the English Throne
events.description: Parliament gathered in Westminster as Richard II was deposed. Henry Bolingbroke, Duke of Lancaster, was proclaimed King of England. The Duchy of Lancaster merged with the crown.
events.significance: Henry's accession began the Lancastrian dynasty. His claim, which rested on force as much as on lineage, shaped the dynastic struggles that later became the Wars of the Roses.

events.title: Mozart's The Magic Flute Premieres
events.description: Mozart conducted the first performance of his final opera, The Magic Flute. It was staged at the Freihaus-Theater auf der Wieden in Vienna, only about two months before his death.
events.significance: The Magic Flute is one of the most beloved works in the opera repertoire. It is also a landmark of German-language opera.

events.title: Britain's First Tram Service Begins
events.description: The first street tram service in the United Kingdom began running in Birkenhead, Merseyside.
events.significance: Trams gave growing industrial cities an affordable way to move people. They helped shape modern urban public transport.

events.title: Riots Over James Meredith's Enrollment at Ole Miss
events.description: Rioting broke out at the University of Mississippi in an attempt to stop James Meredith from enrolling as its first Black student. Two people died.
events.significance: The episode became a defining confrontation of the American civil rights movement. It showed how far federal authorities would go to enforce desegregation.

events.title: Botswana Gains Independence
events.description: The Bechuanaland Protectorate became independent from the United Kingdom as Botswana. Seretse Khama became its first president.
events.significance: Botswana went on to become one of Africa's most stable democracies. It is still celebrated each year on Botswana's Independence Day.
